note: Read from developers.cloudflare.com on the date above. Limits and prices change; re-check before a cost model or a design that sits near a limit. Products renamed in 2026 are listed under their current name with the old one in formerly. Entries with their own checkedAt were read on that date instead.

entries.name: Workers
facts: Paid: 128 MB memory per isolate, CPU up to 5 min per invocation (default 30 s), 10,000 subrequests per invocation by default (configurable up to 10M), 6 simultaneous outgoing connections per request.
Free: 10 ms CPU, 50 subrequests.

entries.name: Durable Objects (SQLite storage)
facts: Paid: rows read 25 billion per month included then $0.001 per million; rows written 50 million included then $1.00 per million; stored data 5 GB-month included then $0.20 per GB-month. Compute billed as requests and wall-clock duration (128 MB per object, shared if co-located).
WebSocket hibernation avoids duration charges while sockets are idle.
SqlStorageCursor reports rowsRead and rowsWritten per statement; these are the billed figures.
Overloaded objects answer 'Durable Object is overloaded' under extreme per-object request rates.

entries.name: Queues
facts: At-least-once delivery; batches (default 10 messages, 5 s); max_retries default 3; a failed message in a batch retries the batch unless messages are acked individually.
Dead-letter queue optional; without one, messages past max_retries are deleted; a DLQ without a consumer keeps messages 4 days.
About 3 operations per message (write, read, delete) at $0.40 per million after included usage; each retry is a read.

entries.name: Workflows
facts: Durable multi-step execution; step.do retries; step.sleep up to 365 days and waitForEvent; sleeping instances do not hold concurrency.

Paid: 10,000 steps per instance by default (up to 25,000), 50,000 concurrent instances per account, 300 instance creations per second per account and 100 per Workflow, 1 MiB per non-stream step result and per event payload, 1 GB state per instance.
Per-Workflow concurrency limits queue instances rather than reject them.
Instance state and logs retained 7 days by default on Paid (configurable to 30).

entries.name: Basin (Pipelines, Catalog, SQL)
entries.formerly: Cloudflare Data Platform: Pipelines, R2 Data Catalog, R2 SQL
facts: Basin Pipelines ingests over HTTP, Workers bindings and Logpush, transforms with SQL, and writes Iceberg tables, Parquet or JSON to R2. Ingress free; transforms $0.04 per GB; sinks $0.03 per GB JSON, $0.06 per GB Parquet/Iceberg; 50 GB per month each included on Paid.
Basin Catalog manages Iceberg tables (compaction, snapshot expiry) readable by external engines (DuckDB, Spark, Snowflake, PyIceberg).
Basin SQL queries Iceberg tables, with joins and subqueries; $2.50 per TB of compressed data scanned (10 MB minimum per query, 10 GB per month included).

entries.name: Workers Analytics Engine
facts: Up to 20 blobs, 20 doubles and 1 index per data point; 16 KB of blobs per point; 250 data points per invocation; 3 months retention.
Adaptive sampling at write time and query time: aggregate metrics, not exact event exploration.

entries.name: R2
facts: Object storage without egress fees; not a query engine on its own.
unverified: Per-operation prices were not re-read for this catalog.

entries.name: D1
facts: Serverless SQLite; rows read and written priced as Durable Objects SQLite; 100 bound parameters and 100 KB per statement; read replicas.
1,000 queries per Worker invocation on Paid.

entries.name: Workers KV
facts: Eventually consistent; 1 write per second to the same key; 1,000 operations per invocation.
entries.guidance: Use directly for read-heavy public metadata or caches when justified; not a transactional store.

entries.name: Vectorize
facts: Paid plan only.
unverified: Index limits and pricing were not re-read for this catalog.

entries.name: Workers Logs
facts: 7 days retention; 5 billion logs per account per day before 1% sampling; 256 KB per log.

entries.name: Artifacts
facts: Git-compatible versioned storage: repositories managed through a Workers binding or REST API (create, import, fork, delete, repo-scoped tokens, file reads by path, commit history) and read and written by any Git client over HTTPS.
Event subscriptions through Queues: repo.created, repo.deleted, repo.forked, repo.imported, and per-repo pushed, cloned, fetched.
Workers Builds can build and deploy from an Artifacts repo; pushes to other branches create Worker Previews. CI Workflows can run on push events.

Limits: 1 GB storage per repo for repos created on or after 2026-09-29 (10 GB before), 1 TB per account (raisable), 2,000 Git requests per 10 s per repo, 2,000 control-plane requests per 10 s per namespace, unlimited repos and namespaces. Namespaces can be pinned to the EU or US.

Workers Paid only. Billing from 2026-11-19: 10,000 operations per month included then $0.15 per 1,000; 1 GB-mo included then $0.50 per GB-mo. A per-repository charge (100,000 included, then $0.01 each) is announced but not yet billed.
Local development: wrangler dev, the Vite plugin and the Workers Vitest integration use a local simulator by default; needs Git 2.32+.

entries.name: Worker Previews
facts: The recommended way to test a branch before production: npx wrangler preview creates or updates a Preview with its own URL under the same Worker.

Preview settings live in a previews block in the Wrangler file (required, may be empty); point preview bindings at staging or test resources. Durable Objects and Containers get isolated resources per Preview.
Version URLs (wrangler versions upload) run one uploaded version against production resources; use them only to inspect a version before deploying it, not for branch testing.
Wrangler environments (wrangler deploy --env <name>) create separately named, persistent Workers: the shape for a long-lived staging.
Workers Builds runs npx wrangler preview for non-production branches by default and can post the Preview URL on the pull request.

toCheck: K2 / K2 Streams (durable logs): a candidate ingestion buffer for error and event intake; not yet read.
Email Service: TapeDB's mailer uses its send_email binding (beta when TapeDB adopted it).
